name: Menopause Japanese
summary: A week of real Japanese home cooking: grilled and simmered fish, tofu, natto and edamame, small bowls of miso soup and barley rice. Built for women over 50, with plenty of calcium and 25 g or more of protein at every meal.
howItWorks:
**Calcium and protein.** Calcium-set tofu appears in most meals, joined by fortified soy milk, sesame, komatsuna, shirasu and the soft bones of canned salmon: about 1,000 to 1,800 mg of calcium a day from food. Every meal has a proper serving of protein. If you've had a hormone-sensitive cancer, ask your care team how much soy suits you.

**Fish, vitamin D and omega-3.** Salmon on Tuesday and Sunday and mackerel on Thursday, plus canned salmon on Monday, bring omega-3 and some vitamin D. A few drops of egoma (perilla) oil add plant omega-3 on the fish-free days. Vitamin D is still hard to get from food, so the note on this plan matters. Fish is always cooked fresh, never a leftover.

**Fibre and low-salt seasoning.** Mugi-gohan (rice cooked with pearled barley), oats, root vegetables, greens and edamame supply the fibre. Bonito and shiitake do the umami work, and reduced-sodium soy sauce and miso go in by the teaspoon. Seaweed is left out because kombu and wakame are very high in iodine.

**Iodine and vitamin K.** Iodine runs low on most days, with a light hand on salt and no seaweed. Iodized salt, fish and eggs give some, so ask your provider about a supplement. If you take warfarin, leave out the natto, which is very rich in a long-lasting form of vitamin K, and keep the leafy greens steady. Your care team can tell you more.

**Cook once, eat twice.** Monday's hambagu, Wednesday's chikuzen-ni, Friday's sukiyaki and Saturday's gyoza each make two portions for the next day's lunch. At Light, the second snack drops away, the soba and gyoza wrappers shrink to about half, the rice gets a little smaller and the chikuzen-ni has less chicken, while the fish, tofu and eggs stay about the same.

recipes.name: Natto and tamagoyaki rice bowl with tofu miso soup
recipes.inspiredBy: Japanese asa-gohan, the classic breakfast tray
recipes.about: Warm rice topped with sticky natto, a soft rolled omelette and a small bowl of tofu miso soup. It is a proper Japanese breakfast that takes under 20 minutes. The **natto, egg and tofu** give you a solid hit of protein before you leave the house.

ingredients.note: calcium-set (the label says calcium sulfate), cubed

steps: Cook the rice and barley ahead (see the tip) and reheat a portion until steaming hot, 74 °C.
Put the bonito flakes in a small pot with a cup of water. Bring to a simmer for 2 minutes, strain, and return the broth to the pot.
Add the tofu to the broth and warm for 2 minutes. Take the pot off the heat, stir the miso in through a small sieve, and add half the scallion. Do not boil the soup once the miso is in.

Beat the egg with a few drops of the soy sauce and the iodized salt. Pour a thin layer into an oiled small pan over medium-low heat, roll it up as it sets, then pour in the rest and roll again until the omelette is firm all the way through. Slice it.

Spoon the rice into a bowl. Stir the natto briskly with the rest of the soy sauce and a few drops of egoma oil until it is sticky and spoon it on top with the omelette and the remaining scallion. Serve with the soup.
recipes.tip: On Sunday, cook about 2 cups (370 g) of brown rice and 1⅓ cups (280 g) of pearled barley together, a little less at Light. That is every rice bowl of the week except the okayu. Simmer them in a big pot of water, like pasta, for 35 to 40 minutes until tender, then drain. Cool within 1 hour in shallow containers, keep 3 days' worth in the fridge and freeze the rest in portions. Reheat from frozen, or thaw in the fridge overnight, until steaming hot, 74 °C, and only once. On warfarin? Skip the natto and add a second egg to the omelette.

recipes.name: Egg, tofu and shirasu okayu with komatsuna
recipes.inspiredBy: Japanese okayu, the gentle rice porridge
recipes.about: A soft, savoury rice porridge with silky tofu, a set egg, tiny shirasu fish and bright greens. It is comforting, and quick if you start from cooked rice (see the tip). **Shirasu are eaten whole, bones and all**, and the tofu is calcium-set, so it starts the day with calcium.

ingredients.note: calcium-set (the label says calcium sulfate), cubed

steps: Rinse the rice and put it in a pot with about six times its volume of water and the ginger. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low for about 1 hour, stirring now and then, until the grains are very soft and the porridge is thick. Rinse and chop the komatsuna while it cooks.
Add the shirasu and the tofu and simmer for 3 minutes so the fish are cooked through and hot.
Stir in the komatsuna, then pour in the beaten egg in a thin stream and stir gently. Cook for 1 to 2 minutes, until the egg is completely set.
Ladle into a bowl, season with the salt, drizzle with the soy sauce and top with the scallion and sesame.
recipes.tip: Use 120 g of cooked rice with 300 ml of water and it is ready in 15 minutes. If you use dried chirimen jako instead of shirasu, pour boiling water over it and drain first: it is salty. Opened tofu keeps in fresh water in the fridge for up to 2 days.

recipes.name: Kinako soy milk oatmeal with mikan
recipes.about: Creamy oats cooked in soy milk with nutty kinako, walnuts and juicy mikan. It tastes a little like a Japanese sweet. The **soy milk and kinako** carry the protein, and the walnuts add plant omega-3.
steps: Put the oats and soy milk in a pot over medium heat. Stir often for about 5 minutes, until thick and creamy.
Whisk the kinako into the porridge off the heat so it does not clump.
Spoon into a bowl, top with the mikan segments and walnuts and drizzle with the honey.

recipes.name: Canned salmon, edamame and sesame rice bowl
recipes.about: Flaked canned salmon with its soft bones, sweet edamame and crisp cucumber over barley rice, dressed with ginger, rice vinegar and sesame. It is cold-friendly and comes together in 15 minutes if the rice is ready. The **soft salmon bones add calcium**, and the salmon brings vitamin D.
steps: Boil the frozen edamame in unsalted water for 3 minutes, drain, cool and shell them. Warm the cooked rice and barley until steaming hot, 74 °C, then let it cool a little.
Rinse the cucumber and scrub the carrot. Whisk the rice vinegar, soy sauce and ginger together in a small bowl. Toss the cucumber and carrot with half of it and leave for 5 minutes.
Mash the salmon with a fork, bones included, and stir in the rest of the dressing.
Pile the rice into a bowl. Top with the salmon, edamame, cucumber and carrot, and scatter over the scallion and sesame.
recipes.tip: Taking it to work? Skip the reheating, use rice straight from the fridge, and pack it with an ice pack until lunch.

recipes.name: Hiyashi soba with chilled tofu and edamame
recipes.inspiredBy: Japanese hiyashi soba and zaru soba
recipes.about: Cold buckwheat noodles with creamy tofu, edamame and cucumber with a light bonito sauce poured over. It is refreshing and filling. The **tofu, egg and edamame give the protein**, and the noodles are boiled in unsalted water to keep the sodium down.

ingredients.note: dried, check the label for salt
calcium-set (the label says calcium sulfate), cubed

steps: Simmer the bonito flakes in half a cup of water for 2 minutes, strain, and stir in the soy sauce, rice vinegar and honey. Set the pan in a bowl of cold water to cool the sauce while you do the rest.

Boil the frozen edamame in unsalted water for 3 minutes, drain, cool and shell. Boil the soba in plenty of unsalted water as the packet says, then rinse well under cold water, rubbing gently, and drain. Choose a soba with little or no added salt.
Rinse the spinach and cucumber. Plunge the spinach into boiling unsalted water for 1 minute, cool in cold water, squeeze dry and cut into short lengths.
Beat the egg and cook it in a thin layer in a lightly oiled non-stick pan until completely set, then slice into ribbons.
Put the noodles in a bowl and arrange the tofu, edamame, spinach, egg ribbons and cucumber on top.
Pour over the cold sauce, drizzle with the egoma oil and finish with the ginger, scallion and sesame.
recipes.tip: Egoma (perilla) oil is sold at Korean grocers as deulgireum; flaxseed oil is used the same way. Keep either in the fridge and never heat it. At smaller sizes the noodles shrink to a small nest, and the tofu and edamame carry the bowl.

recipes.name: Shrimp and egg donburi with komatsuna
recipes.about: Plump shrimp and softly set egg simmered in a light bonito and soy broth over barley rice, with a handful of greens. It is quick and warming. The **shrimp and egg** carry the protein.

ingredients.note: peeled and deveined; if frozen, thaw in the fridge overnight and cook within 2 days

steps: Rinse the komatsuna before cutting it. Reheat the cooked rice and barley until steaming hot, 74 °C, and spoon into a bowl.
Simmer the bonito in half a cup of water for 2 minutes, strain, and return it to the pan with the soy sauce, honey and onion. Cook for 3 minutes until the onion is soft.
Add the shrimp and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until they are pink and opaque all the way through. Add the komatsuna for the last minute.
Pour the egg over in a thin stream. Cover and cook for 1 to 2 minutes, until the egg is completely set.
Slide everything over the rice with the broth.

recipes.name: Tofu and chicken hambagu with grated daikon and komatsuna
recipes.about: Tender patties of minced chicken thigh and calcium-set tofu, served with refreshing grated daikon, a vinegar-soy sauce and sesame komatsuna. The tofu keeps them light and moist. The **tofu and komatsuna bring calcium** and the patties carry plenty of protein.

ingredients.note: calcium-set (the label says calcium sulfate), squeezed in a cloth

steps: Cook the rice and barley (see the breakfast tip) and keep warm. This recipe makes two portions. Scrub and rinse the daikon and komatsuna, then grate the daikon.

Squeeze the tofu in a clean cloth until it is firm and crumbly, then mash it in a bowl. Add the chicken, onion, egg, ginger, the iodized salt and a third of the soy sauce and mix with your hand until sticky. Shape into two oval patties, pressing the centre thin. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw chicken.

Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Cook the patties for 4 minutes on each side, then cover and cook for another 5 minutes, until a thermometer in the centre reads 74 °C, with no pink and clear juices.
Boil the komatsuna in unsalted water for 1 minute, cool in cold water, squeeze dry and toss with half the sesame and a little soy sauce.

Squeeze the grated daikon lightly. Mix the rice vinegar with the remaining soy sauce. Serve the patties with daikon on top, the sauce spooned over, the greens and the rice. Cool the second portion and refrigerate within 2 hours for tomorrow's lunch, then reheat until steaming hot throughout, 74 °C.
recipes.tip: No komatsuna? Baby bok choy works the same way.

recipes.name: Grilled salmon with spinach goma-ae and daikon miso soup
recipes.about: A simple grilled salmon fillet with sesame-dressed spinach, a small bowl of daikon miso soup and mugi-gohan. It is the classic Japanese dinner in one tray. The **salmon brings omega-3 and vitamin D**.

ingredients.note: scrubbed and cut into thin matchsticks

steps: Cook the rice and barley ahead if you have not (see the breakfast tip) and reheat a portion until steaming hot, 74 °C.

Pat the salmon dry and rub it with the salt, then wash your hands and board after handling the raw fish. Grill or broil it, skin side up, for about 5 minutes, turn and cook for another 4 to 5 minutes, until the fish reaches 70 °C and flakes easily.
Rinse the spinach well. Plunge the spinach into boiling unsalted water for 1 minute, cool in cold water and squeeze dry. Toss with the ground sesame, soy sauce, rice vinegar and honey.

Simmer the bonito in a cup of water for 2 minutes and strain. Add the daikon and simmer for 5 minutes, until it turns translucent. Off the heat, stir the miso in through a small sieve and add the scallion.
Serve the salmon with the spinach, the soup and the rice.

recipes.name: Chikuzen-ni, simmered chicken with root vegetables
recipes.about: Chicken thigh simmered with lotus root, kabocha, carrot, shiitake and edamame in a light soy and ginger broth, glossy and not too sweet. It is even better the next day. It is a **fibre-rich simmered dish** with plenty of protein.

ingredients.note: kabocha or buttercup squash, seeded, cut into chunks
soaked until soft, stems removed, quartered

steps: Cook the rice and barley (see the breakfast tip) and keep warm. This recipe makes two portions.

Soak the dried shiitake in 250 ml of warm water for 30 minutes and keep the soaking water. Scrub and rinse the lotus root, kabocha and carrot. Soak the lotus root slices in cold water for 5 minutes, then drain.

Heat the oil in a wide pot over medium heat and brown the chicken for 4 minutes. Wash your hands and board after cutting the raw chicken. Add the lotus root, carrot, shiitake and ginger and stir for 2 minutes.

Add about 200 ml of the shiitake soaking water, the soy sauce, the salt and the honey. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook for 10 minutes, then lay the kabocha on top, cover again and cook for another 10 minutes, until the vegetables are tender and the chicken reaches 74 °C with no pink.
Add the edamame, then uncover and simmer for 5 minutes, spooning the broth over, until it has reduced to a glaze.
Serve over the rice. Cool the second portion and refrigerate within 2 hours for tomorrow's lunch, and reheat until steaming hot throughout, 74 °C.

recipes.name: Mackerel simmered in miso and ginger with spinach
recipes.about: Mackerel fillets simmered gently with ginger and a spoonful of miso, with cubes of tofu in the same pot and a bright spinach ohitashi. The miso sauce is thin and savoury, not heavy. The **mackerel is rich in omega-3**, and the tofu adds calcium.

ingredients.note: fillet, cut in two; Atlantic or Pacific, never king mackerel
calcium-set (the label says calcium sulfate), cubed

steps: Cook the rice and barley ahead if you have not (see the breakfast tip) and reheat a portion until steaming hot, 74 °C.
Pour boiling water over the mackerel in a sieve for a few seconds to rinse away any fishy smell, and pat dry. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw fish.

In a small wide pan, bring 100 ml of water, the ginger, honey and half the miso to a simmer. Lay in the mackerel, skin side up, and the tofu. Cover loosely and simmer for 8 minutes, spooning the liquid over.

Stir the remaining miso with a ladle of the hot liquid and stir it back into the pan with the soy sauce. Simmer for 2 more minutes, until the fish reaches 70 °C and flakes easily and the sauce thickens slightly.
Meanwhile rinse the spinach well and boil it in unsalted water for 1 minute, cool in cold water, squeeze dry, cut into short lengths and top with the bonito flakes and sesame.
Serve the mackerel and tofu with the sauce, the spinach, scallion and rice.

recipes.name: Beef and tofu sukiyaki-style nabe
recipes.about: A shallow pot of lean beef, tofu, cabbage, carrot, shiitake and komatsuna in a gently sweet soy and bonito broth. Everything cooks in one pan and the broth soaks into the rice. It is a **calcium-rich, one-pot dinner**, with the tofu and greens doing most of the work.

ingredients.note: calcium-set (the label says calcium sulfate), cut into slabs

steps: Cook the rice and barley (see the breakfast tip) and keep warm. This recipe makes two portions.

Soak the dried shiitake in 150 ml of warm water for 30 minutes. Simmer the bonito in 200 ml of water for 2 minutes and strain. Add the shiitake and its soaking water, the soy sauce, honey and salt to make the broth.
Rinse the cabbage, carrot and komatsuna. Put the tofu, cabbage, carrot and scallion in a wide shallow pan with the broth. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook for 8 minutes.
Add the soaked shiitake and cook for 3 minutes. Lay the beef slices on top and simmer for 2 to 3 minutes, until no pink remains and the beef is cooked through. Add the komatsuna in the last minute.
Serve over or beside the rice with some of the broth. Cool the second portion and refrigerate within 2 hours for tomorrow's lunch, and reheat until steaming hot throughout, 74 °C.

recipes.name: Pork and tofu gyoza with simmered kabocha
recipes.about: Juicy gyoza filled with lean pork, tofu and cabbage, pan-fried until crisp underneath and steamed until tender, with a vinegar-soy dip and soft simmered kabocha (or buttercup squash). It is a fun weekend project. The **tofu keeps the filling tender** and adds a little calcium.

ingredients.note: calcium-set (the label says calcium sulfate), squeezed in a cloth
kabocha or buttercup squash, seeded, cut into chunks

steps: Cook the brown rice and barley (see the breakfast tip). This recipe makes two portions.
Scrub and rinse the kabocha. Simmer the chunks in a small covered pot with 100 ml of water and a splash of the soy sauce for 12 minutes, until tender but not falling apart.

Squeeze the tofu in a clean cloth until crumbly. Mix the pork, tofu, cabbage, scallion, ginger, garlic and half the soy sauce by hand until sticky. Fry a small spoonful and taste to check the seasoning.

Put a heaped teaspoon of filling in the middle of each wrapper, wet the edge, and fold and pleat to seal. If filling is left when the wrappers run out, shape it into small flat patties and fry them in the pan with the gyoza. Wash your hands and board when the gyoza are folded.

Heat the canola oil in a non-stick pan with a lid. Arrange the gyoza flat side down and fry for 2 minutes, until golden underneath. Add 80 ml of water, cover and steam over medium heat for 6 minutes, then uncover and cook until the water is gone. Cut one open, and a patty if you made them, to check: the pork must reach 71 °C with no pink.
Mix the vinegar and the rest of the soy sauce for the dip.

Serve the gyoza with the dip, the kabocha drizzled with the egoma oil, and the rice. Cool the second portion and refrigerate within 2 hours for tomorrow's lunch, and reheat in a covered pan with a splash of water until steaming hot throughout, 74 °C.
recipes.tip: Freeze uncooked gyoza on a tray, then bag them; cook from frozen with a little more water.

recipes.name: Salmon chanchan-yaki with cabbage and mushrooms
recipes.about: Salmon steamed on a bed of cabbage, carrot and shiitake with a thin miso glaze, all in one pan. It is sweet, savoury and very easy. The **salmon brings omega-3 and vitamin D**, and the vegetables add fibre.

ingredients.note: calcium-set (the label says calcium sulfate), cubed

steps: Cook the rice and barley ahead if you have not (see the breakfast tip) and reheat a portion until steaming hot, 74 °C.
Soak the dried shiitake in warm water for 30 minutes, then slice them and keep 3 tablespoons of the water. Whisk the miso, honey and the soaking water into a smooth glaze.
Rinse the cabbage and scrub the carrot. Heat the oil in a wide pan with a lid. Spread the onion, carrot, cabbage and shiitake in a layer.

Lay the salmon and the tofu on top and spoon over the glaze. Cover and steam over medium-low heat for 12 minutes, until the salmon reaches 70 °C and flakes easily and the vegetables are tender. Wash your hands and board after handling the raw fish.
Scatter with the sesame and serve with the rice, spooning the juices over.

recipes.name: Steamed kabocha with sesame
recipes.about: Soft steamed kabocha (or buttercup squash), naturally sweet, with a sprinkle of toasted sesame and a few drops of soy sauce, a very Japanese way to eat squash. It brings **vitamin A and fibre** to the afternoon.

ingredients.note: kabocha or buttercup squash, seeded, cut into chunks

steps: Scrub and rinse the kabocha. Steam the chunks over simmering water for 12 to 15 minutes, until a knife slides in easily.
Toss with the sesame and soy sauce and serve warm.

recipes.name: Warm kinako soy milk
recipes.about: A warm mug of soy milk whisked with nutty kinako and a little honey. It is **calcium and soy protein** in a cup.
steps: Warm the soy milk in a small pot until steaming, not boiling.
Whisk in the kinako and honey until smooth and pour into a mug.

recipes.name: Persimmon and almonds
recipes.about: Sweet autumn persimmon with a small handful of almonds for crunch. Almonds are a modern snack here rather than a traditional one, but they are an easy way to get **vitamin E**.
steps: Slice the persimmon and serve with the almonds.

recipes.name: Mikan and almonds
recipes.about: A juicy mikan with a handful of almonds. Almonds are a modern addition, there for **vitamin E**, and the mikan brings vitamin C.
steps: Peel the mikan and serve with the almonds.

recipes.name: Plain yogurt with kinako and almonds
recipes.about: Tangy yogurt with nutty kinako, chopped almonds and a spoonful of honey. Almonds are a modern touch, there for **vitamin E**, and the yogurt adds calcium.
steps: Spoon the yogurt into a bowl, dust with the kinako, scatter over the almonds and drizzle with the honey.

recipes.name: Edamame with sesame salt
recipes.about: Edamame tossed with toasted sesame and a pinch of iodized salt, like the sesame salt (goma-jio) served at home. It is a **plant protein and calcium** snack.
steps: Boil the frozen edamame in unsalted water for 3 minutes, drain and let them cool a little.
Toss with the sesame and iodized salt.

recipes.name: Warm almond kinako soy milk
recipes.about: Warm soy milk whisked with kinako and finely ground almonds, lightly sweet and nutty. Almonds are a modern touch, there for **vitamin E**, and the soy milk adds calcium.
steps: Grind the almonds finely in a clean spice grinder or with a mortar.
Warm the soy milk in a small pot until steaming, not boiling.
Whisk in the kinako, almonds and honey until smooth and pour into a mug.

recipes.name: Edamame with a pinch of salt
recipes.about: A bowl of warm edamame, a favourite Japanese snack. They are a **plant protein and fibre** snack.
steps: Boil the frozen edamame in unsalted water for 3 minutes, drain and let them cool a little.
Toss with the iodized salt.

recipes.name: Soy-marinated egg
recipes.about: A hard-boiled egg marinated in diluted soy sauce, the kind found in every bento. It is a **small bite of protein**.
steps: Boil the egg in water for 10 minutes, until the yolk is completely set. Cool in cold water and peel. Boiling for Tuesday? Boil a second egg for Sunday and keep it in its shell in the fridge.
Mix the soy sauce, honey and 2 tablespoons of water in a small bowl, add the egg and marinate in the fridge for at least 2 hours, turning once. Eat within 2 days.
